scope: The exact FE-356 claim derived from arXiv:2608.17684: in the paper's simulated AgentDojo Banking audit on Qwen 3.7 Flash, SkillOpt self-evolution under matched benign acquisition trajectories raises benign utility from 0.741 to 0.837 while injected-content exposure rises from 0.820 to 0.943 and unauthorized financial-state change rises from 0.583 to 0.685. Conditional attack success among exposed episodes falls from 0.605 to 0.562 while total ASR rises from 0.496 to 0.530 because exposure increases. Across three independently evolved lineages, capability, exposure, and unauthorized-state change increase in all three while total ASR increases in only two. This grade is bounded to that executor, setting, method and three-lineage experiment; it does not establish that self-evolution generally worsens safety or isolate representation alone from SkillOpt's full admission/write/update mechanism.

independent_checks.logical_consistency_result: The sealed FE-356 summary agrees with the primary arXiv record on the direction and reported magnitudes of the central SkillOpt result: utility and exposure rise, conditional susceptibility among exposed episodes falls, overall ASR nevertheless rises, and execution-grounded unauthorized financial-state change increases. The three-lineage result supports the narrower point that aggregate ASR can hide a consistent exposure/unauthorized-effect drift because ASR itself rises in only two lineages. The study is author-run and setting-bounded; the three lineages are internal independent evolution runs, not external replication, and the end-to-end SkillOpt treatment does not identify representation as the unique causal component.

grading.independent_replication: not_established; three independently evolved lineages are internal study replications, not an external third-party reproduction
grading.reproducibility: moderate_to_strong_for_the_reported sealed-endpoint experiment; external reproduction was not independently verified in this slice
grading.primary_source_support: strong; the arXiv record directly reports the central utility, exposure, conditional-ASR, overall-ASR, unauthorized-state-change and three-lineage pattern
grading.uncertainty: The evidence strongly supports the narrow measurement lesson that post-evolution utility and aggregate ASR are insufficient summaries in this tested financial-agent setting: exposure/contact rate, conditional susceptibility and execution-grounded unauthorized effects can move differently. It does not establish the prevalence of this pattern across self-evolution methods, models, domains or deployed systems, nor does it isolate representation, admission policy, write policy or update mechanics as the unique cause.

phase1_acceptance_boundary: FE-356 contributes bounded evidence for the aggregate usefulness/false-completion guard: a parity or self-improvement route should not be accepted from utility or aggregate ASR alone when exposure, conditional susceptibility and execution-grounded unauthorized effects can diverge. It does not itself eliminate a Work/protected/manual execution dependency, prove a zero-quota Chat-native outcome route, establish 18/18 current-pool coverage, satisfy replay/resume or scheduler-persistence gates, or close the Phase-1 root.
